Its only appearance in the same-level transverse source is $-(B_p\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$, which does not differentiate $B_p$. The formal statement admits the broader parent pressure class of Section 5.1.

p5.2.mean-coefficient-powers|TorusEuler..annotation: Put $F=D_aX$. The kinetic metric $K=F^TF$ and the skew coefficient $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$ involve only products of the already estimated parent coefficients. A derivative of order $m$ distributes among those factors with total order $m$. Thus Equation (D.6) persists with a fixed linear exponent in $m$, before the weights $\ell_*^m$ are applied.

p5.2.inverse-constant-power|TorusEuler.P.annotation: The constant $A$ in Equation (4.10) bounds the inverse of the two-endpoint equation. In its formula the inverse deformation and low-order norms of $M,K,\Omega$ are bounded by parent powers before choosing $\ell_*$. Choosing the radius afterward is important: the factor $\ell_*^{1/2}$ in Equation (5.13) must offset an inverse norm which does not itself grow as the radius shrinks.

p5.2.radius-threshold|TorusEuler.exists_.annotation: The derivatives of positive order have a small factor in Lemma D.2(c): $\ell_*^m|K|_m\lesssim_m\mathsf D^C\ell_*$, and likewise for $\Omega$. Passing to the half-Hölder norm costs $\ell_*^{-1/2}$ by Equation (D.2), leaving the factor $\sqrt{\ell_*}$. The formal coefficient bound makes this explicit as a parent factor $\mathsf D^9\sqrt{\ell_*}$, times order-dependent constants.

p5.2.radius-threshold|TorusEuler.Paper.S.annotation: For a label derivative, the highest derivative of $v$ still has coefficients $K$ and $\Omega$. Only terms in which at least one derivative falls on a coefficient are moved to the datum. Thus Equation (5.13) is a smallness condition on positive-order weighted coefficient derivatives; it does not require the metric $K$ or the skew term $\Omega$ to be small.

p5.2.radius-threshold|TorusEuler.Paper.T.annotation: At first order the new term in the datum is $(\partial_aK)v$. Applying the inverse after weighting it by $\ell_*$ costs at most $C A\ell_*|K|_{1,1/2}\|v\|_{[0],1/2}$. By Equation (5.13) this is bounded by an absolute multiple of the preceding order. At higher orders the inverse factor $A$ is similarly paired with the weight belonging to the derivatives that fall on $K$.

p5.2.radius-threshold|TorusEuler.Paper.P.annotation: One can see the remaining radius factor directly: Lemma D.2(c) at order $m$ and $m+1$ bounds the two terms on the right of Equation (D.2) by $C_m\mathsf D^C\ell_*$. Multiplication by $\ell_*^{-1/2}$ leaves the half power of $\ell_*$. The final scalar inequality absorbs $A$ after its bound has been obtained.

p5.2.derivative-lifting|TorusEuler.paper.annotation: For each label derivative the differentiated displacement has the same two zero endpoints and remains solenoidal. The derivatives of $c$ are time-independent and the differentiated pressure term is again a label gradient. Thus the same endpoint inverse applies. Every commutator of order $n$ contains at least one derivative of a coefficient and at most $n-1$ derivatives of the unknown, as required for induction in the proof of Lemma D.3.

p5.2.holder-estimate|TorusEuler.Paper.Te.annotation: The velocity $v=F^{-1}B$ in Equation (5.14) has three label components and is solenoidal. This is the endpoint inverse on the whole slab, not the two-dimensional transverse inverse measured relative to the active seed. Its norm includes the Hölder seminorm at each derivative order through $n$. The Lean statement permits the broader parent pressure class under the residual and coercivity hypotheses.

p5.2.holder-estimate|TorusEuler.Paper.Pr.annotation: Writing $u_n=\|v\|_{[n],1/2}$, the commutator estimate gives $u_n\le C_n(A\|L\|_{[n],1/2}+u_{n-1})$. Indeed Equation (5.13) has already paid for the inverse acting on each differentiated coefficient. Induction from $u_0\le A\|L\|_{[0],1/2}$ therefore retains just one factor $A$; without (5.13) the naive recursion could lose a power of $A$ at each derivative.

p5.2.product-readout|TorusEuler.Paper.Pr.annotation: The two changes of coordinates are $g=F^T\bar f$ on the input and $B=Fv$ on the output. Each uses the same-order Hölder product estimate, and Equations (5.8) and (D.2) bound the deformation factors. Neither change introduces an additional derivative of the unknown. The sole extra derivative of the source in Equation (5.12) comes from replacing its Hölder norm by a supremum norm.

e02.transverse.equation|TorusEuler.Paper.annotation: Centering is necessary: averaging Equation (5.15) gives $\langle f\rangle_s=\partial_t\langle V\rangle_s+M\langle V\rangle_s$, since the pressure derivative integrates to zero. If $\langle V\rangle_s=0$, the force must have zero mean too. The normalized velocity and pressure are specified here; existence comes from the projected ODE.

e02.transverse.pressure-slope|TorusEuler.annotation: Use $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ in the derivative of $\kappa\cdot V=0$. Then $0=-\kappa\cdot MV+\kappa\cdot(f-MV)-|\kappa|^2\partial_s\mathsf p$. The two identical strain terms account for the factor two in Equation (5.16). The nonzero wave vector makes division by $|\kappa|^2$ legitimate.

e02.transverse.activation-endpoint|Torus.annotation: The zero-start condition is at time zero. If $t_0>0$, vanishing of the force on the inactive prefix and continuity of the solution give $V(t_0)=0$; if $t_0=0$, this is the prescribed initial condition. The statement needed for Equation (5.21) is zero velocity at launch, not an independently imposed pressure value.

For positive $t_0$ the inactive condition gives zero at every earlier time, and continuity extends it to $t_0$. For $t_0=0$ there is no such earlier interval, so the conclusion instead uses the initial condition. This justifies dropping the launch contribution in Equation (5.20).

The joint smooth existence theorem preserves the vanishing prefix. In particular its velocity at the activation time is zero, by continuity for positive $t_0$ and by the given launch value when $t_0=0$. This is the property needed to pass from Equation (5.20) to the forced bound (5.21).

e02.transverse.frame-identities|TorusEul.annotation: The two identities express that $A_\perp^\dagger$ is a left inverse on the two coordinates and a projected inverse on the three physical coordinates. In particular $A_\perp^\dagger\kappa=0$. This lets one derive Equation (5.18) directly from Equation (5.15) without first substituting the formula for the phase pressure.

e02.transverse.frame-time|TorusEuler.Loc.annotation: The coefficient in the two-dimensional equation includes the derivative of the moving frame. Substituting $V=A_\perp v$ gives $V_t=A_\perp v_t+MA_\perp v$. Adding the strain $MV$ gives a second copy of $MA_\perp v$; multiplying by $A_\perp^\dagger$ kills the pressure direction and yields Equation (5.18).

e02.lemma53.near-origin|TorusEuler.Local.annotation: The coefficient of the principal Hessian of the leading pressure is $-c_{\mathbf a}F_h'$, where $c_{\mathbf a}=2\widetilde\chi g(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)/|\kappa|^2$. The sign in Equation (5.19) ensures $c_{\mathbf a}\ge0$. Thus the largest positive curvature from that tensor occurs where $F_h'$ is negative, and is bounded by $Chc_{\mathbf a}|\kappa|^2$. Positivity of the coupling is needed on the whole envelope, not just at its center.

e02.lemma53.near-origin|TorusEuler.Paper.annotation: The seed hypothesis is relative: Equation (5.5) controls the propagation of every transverse vector at the origin, not just the selected seed. Together with the positive central coupling margin, it gives Equation (5.19) on a sufficiently small envelope. The numbered Lean statement permits an upper-normalized nonzero central seed rather than requiring the maximum to attain the normalization; it also admits the broader parent pressure class.

The pressure condition is an upper bound as a quadratic form, not a small norm of the Hessian. By Equation (5.19), $0\le c_{\mathbf a}|\kappa|^2\le2|\kappa||M||\mathbf a|\lesssim\mathsf D^3\lambda^{1/4}$. Since $F_h'\ge-Ch$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, its principal Hessian is bounded above by $C\mathsf D^3\lambda^{-1/4}I$. The linked numbered theorem establishes the seed bound and sign used here, with an upper-normalized nonzero central seed.

e02.lemma53.forward-hypotheses|TorusEule.annotation: Part (i) of Lemma 5.3 is an estimate for a given solution of the projected velocity equation with possibly nonzero launch data. Its support assumptions keep every label of interest within reach of the central propagator comparison. The active-profile theorem treats data on $[t_0,T]$ with compatible lattice-phase translations, without assuming a centered force.

The estimate in part (i) of Lemma 5.3 does not require zero initial velocity or a centered forcing, because it concerns the projected ODE alone. The numbered Lean statement assumes full-slab smoothness and then estimates its active restriction; the related active-profile theorem covers data smooth only on the active interval.

e02.lemma53.forward-bound|TorusEuler.Hie.annotation: The term $\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}$ permits two different applications of Equation (5.20). For the leading homogeneous solution the initial data have size proportional to $\gamma(t_0)$; for the forced correction the initial data are zero. The full-slab formal helper measures both on the active interval, and therefore yields the same type of estimate in each case.

e02.lemma53.forward-bound|TorusEuler.Pap.annotation: Integrating a bound using only $|M|\le\mathsf D$ could give an exponential in $\mathsf D$, too costly for the power-separated frequencies. Instead Equation (5.5) supplies a polynomial bound for the central propagator after dividing out the intended amplification. A small envelope transfers it to nearby labels. The numbered formal statement takes full-slab smooth data; the active-profile helper allows smoothness just on $[t_0,T]$.

e02.lemma53.zero-start-hypotheses|TorusE.annotation: The support condition puts the labels of the forced solution in the region where the central propagator estimate extends. The inactive-prefix condition gives $V(t_0)=0$, removing the launch term of Equation (5.20). Centering of the force has a separate role: it yields a centered velocity and a periodic pressure primitive. The mean correction is not required to share this support or time prefix.

r3c8-lemma53-transverse-existence|TorusE.annotation: After solving the velocity ODE there is no remaining freedom in the phase pressure. If two normalized pairs solve the same equation from zero, uniqueness for the velocity and Equation (5.16) give equality of the pressure derivatives; the average removes the integration constant. The linked result proves uniqueness, not existence.

e02.lemma53.transverse-pressure-bound|To.annotation: Equation (5.16) gives $|\partial_s\mathsf p|\le |\kappa|^{-1}(|f|+2|M||V|)$. The inverse wave-vector length provides the factor $\lambda^{-1}$, while taking the normalized phase primitive is bounded at the same scaled derivative order. In particular the pressure does not have to be obtained by inverting a spatial Laplacian on the torus at this step. The full-slab helper gives Equation (5.21) with exponent $20$.

The pressure estimate is later used together with the equation, not by differentiating it twice in physical space. At level two, $\mathsf p_2$ has size $\lambda^{-1-23/12}$ up to parent powers; two physical derivatives could leave $\lambda^{1/12}$. But $\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p_2=P_\kappa(f_2+f_2^S-2MV_2)$ has size $\lambda^{-23/12}$. Only one physical derivative is then needed, leaving $\lambda^{-5/12}$ in the Hessian bound (Equation (5.52)). The numbered Lean estimate allows the broader parent pressure and central-amplitude hypotheses.

e02.lemma53.leading-bound|TorusEuler.Loc.annotation: The factor $h$ in Equation (5.22) is a bound on the phase profile, not on its slope at the origin. Indeed $F_h(0)=0$, $F_h'(0)=1$ and $g(0)=1$ give the central gradient $\mathbf a(t,0)\otimes\kappa(t,0)$ before switching. Thus the velocity can have size $\gamma\lambda^{-5/4}$ while its central gradient has scale $\gamma\lambda^{1/4}$ up to parent powers. The formal estimate uses a fixed admissible envelope.

e02.lemma53.leading-bound|TorusEuler.Pap.annotation: Part (iii) of Lemma 5.3 starts from a nonzero homogeneous seed, not from the zero-start inverse of part (ii) of Lemma 5.3. The bound at launch is proportional to $\gamma(t_0)$, which cancels the launch denominator in Equation (5.20); multiplication by $F_h$ contributes $h$. The numbered formal statement fixes one admissible envelope instead of ranging over all cutoffs in the paper's class.

e02.lemma53.coframe-coefficient-proof|To.annotation: The Gram matrix $K_\perp=A_\perp^TA_\perp$ has eigenvalues between $\mathsf D^{-2}$ and $\mathsf D^2$. Differentiating $K_\perp^{-1}K_\perp=I$ bounds the jets of the inverse, and hence those of $A_\perp^\dagger$ and $\mathcal M_\perp$. These are bounds before multiplication by the radius weights; Equation (D.7) then absorbs the cost of each positive label derivative.

e02.lemma53.forced-integral|TorusEuler.w.annotation: Let $\Phi_a(t,t')$ denote the two-dimensional homogeneous propagator. The preceding estimate bounds $\Phi_a(t,t')$ by $e\mathsf D^3\gamma(t)/\gamma(t')$. Substituting this in the variation-of-constants formula gives Equation (5.23); the denominator in the integrand is $\gamma(t')$, not $\gamma(t)$. Thus even a very small early forcing is measured in relation to the early seed, and amplification from that time is already included.

e02.lemma53.near-seed-comparison|TorusEu.annotation: In the fixed coordinates, the difference $v_a-v_0$ has initial value $(A_\perp^\dagger(t_0,a)-A_\perp^\dagger(t_0,0))\mathbf a(t_0,0)$, and force $-(\mathcal M_\perp(t,a)-\mathcal M_\perp(t,0))v_a$. Both coefficient differences are bounded by a parent power times $|a|$. After applying Equation (5.23), return to the physical vectors by writing $\mathbf a(t,a)-\mathbf a(t,0)=A_\perp(t,a)(v_a-v_0)+(A_\perp(t,a)-A_\perp(t,0))v_0$. This retains the factor $|\mathbf a(t,0)|$. The Lean conclusion records the comparison with a coefficient depending on the parent bound.

The comparison is required relative to the central seed at every active time. This is what permits the initial projection and coefficient variation to be small even when the central seed is far below its terminal size. A uniform absolute error would not suffice to retain the positive coupling margin in Equation (5.5). The definition does not supply the bound on its comparison coefficient.

e02.lemma53.pressure-coefficient-route|T.annotation: The normalization matters when differentiating in the labels: $\kappa/\lambda$ and $|\kappa/\lambda|^{-2}$ have bounds independent of $\lambda$ in Equation (5.8). Thus all the explicit frequency gain can be kept in $\mathsf p$ as a factor $\lambda^{-1}$. The coefficient lemma supplies the jet bounds for this product; the pressure estimate also uses the phase primitive.

e02.lemma53.leading-proof-route|TorusEul.annotation: At $t_0$ the initial value for the homogeneous estimate is $g(I-P_\kappa)\mathbf a(t_0,0)$. Its scaled norm contains $|\mathbf a(t_0,0)|=\gamma(t_0)\lambda^{-3/4}$, so the small denominator in Equation (5.20) cancels. The factor $F_h$ contributes a further $h$ only after estimating $g\mathbf a$; this is the origin of $\lambda^{-5/4}$ in Equation (5.22).

e02.hierarchy.first-mean-source|TorusEul.annotation: The abstract pre-mean source at $p=2$ contains the material derivative of the stored completion of $V_1$, the slow gradient of its pressure and the two quadratic interactions. It subtracts the completion of the activation error at that level. With the cutoff identities this gives precisely the switched linear term in Equation (5.25).

e02.hierarchy.mean-fast-integration|Toru.annotation: This stress calculation extends to later levels. In Equation (5.26), averaging a fast pair with $i+j=p+1$ gives $\langle(\mathbf d\cdot V_{i-1})Y_j\rangle_s$, whose indices add to $p$. Since $C_i$ is a slow curl, $\mathbf d\cdot Y_i=\mathbf d\cdot V_i$. After reindexing, the averaged fast terms therefore complete the slow oscillatory products to row divergences of $\langle Y_j\otimes Y_i\rangle_s$. This is the identity underlying the improved mean estimate (5.35).

e02.hierarchy.general-pre-source|TorusEu.annotation: At level three the slow products are $(Z_1\cdot\mathbf d)Z_2+(Z_2\cdot\mathbf d)Z_1$. The fast products are $(C_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_2+(C_3\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$. Both use only earlier oscillations and means, since $C_3=C[V_2]$. The linear terms carry the completion of $V_2$ and the slow gradient of its pressure to the next level. This is the general indexing in Equation (5.26).

e02.hierarchy.sources|TorusEuler.Paper.S.annotation: Adding the prescribed mean and transverse sources gives $\bar f_p+f_p=-H_p$ for $p\ge3$ and $-H_2-R_U\circ X$ for $p=2$. These are exactly the negatives of the known errors before the new mean starts transporting the earlier phases. The supplementary source then cancels the additional phase products. This split is the cancellation of the momentum residual through level $p$ in Equation (5.29).

e02.hierarchy.supplementary-source|Torus.annotation: The only new mean in Equation (5.28) occurs in $-(B_p\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$; all differentiated oscillations are already known. It is important here that the mean has the improved bound. If $S_p=\lambda^{-5/4-2(p-1)/3}$, the ordinary level bound $B_p=O(S_p)$ would give a fast product of size $\lambda^{1/4}S_p$ up to parent powers. The stronger induction bound $O(\lambda^{-1/2}S_p)$ instead gives $\lambda^{-1/4}S_p$. The phase mean of the product is zero.

The indices of the fast mean interactions satisfy $i+j=p+1$, $i\ge2$, $j\ge1$. The allowed pairs can therefore be enumerated by $2\le i\le p$, with $j=p+1-i$. The endpoint $i=p$ pairs the current mean with $Y_1=V_1$; the linked equality is for the positive advection, so Equation (5.28) has a minus sign.

e02.hierarchy.transverse-after-mean|Toru.annotation: The new mean enters the transverse equation only in the now known supplementary force. Both $f_p$ and $f_p^S$ are centered, and the preceding oscillations make their sum vanish outside the envelope and on the inactive prefix. Thus the zero-start transverse inverse can be applied once to the entire force, with the pressure determined afterward by Equation (5.16). There is no coupled same-level iteration.

e02.prop54.well-defined|TorusEuler.Paper.annotation: At level $p$ the last correction already known is $C_p=C[V_{p-1}]$. It is the only level-$p$ field in $H_p$. The mean inverse applied to Equation (5.27) therefore determines $B_p$ before Equation (5.28) is formed; the transverse inverse and curl then determine $V_p,\mathsf p_p,C_{p+1}$. This also shows that increasing the final depth does not change the lower levels. The formal proposition asserts existence of the seed and uniqueness for fixed seed and normalized pressures.

e02.prop54.velocity-pressure-sums|TorusE.annotation: The phase derivative of $\bar q_p$ vanishes. The phase derivative of $\mathsf p_p$ enforces $\kappa\cdot V_p=0$ in Equation (5.15), while its label gradient is left for the next level. In particular the label gradient of $\mathsf p_P$ remains in Equation (5.30), even though $\mathsf p_P$ is included in the pressure sum.

e02.prop54.divergence|TorusEuler.Paper.S.annotation: With $V_0=V_{P+1}=0$, Equation (3.6) gives $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot Z_i=\mathbf d\cdot V_i-\mathbf d\cdot V_{i-1}$ for $1\le i\le P+1$. Here the slow divergence of the curl $C_i$ and of the mean $B_i$ are both zero. Summing telescopes, with $Z_{P+1}=C_{P+1}$ providing the last cancellation. The proof uses the equivalent sum of completed curls.

e02.prop54.residual|TorusEuler.Paper.Sta.annotation: The residual of the parent is a function of $(t,a)$ alone after composition with $X$. It belongs entirely to the mean source at level two, with sign $-R_U\circ X$ in Equation (5.27). Its cancellation in Equation (5.29) is therefore pointwise in the independent phase as well as on the physical graph. The next residual consists only of the tail and the activation term.

e02.prop54.vanishing-prefix|TorusEuler.P.annotation: For $p\ge2$ the transverse correction vanishes at $t_0$: by the vanishing prefix if $t_0>0$, and by its initial condition if $t_0=0$. In Equation (5.20) the term $\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V_p(t_0)\|_{[n]}$ is therefore zero. At the level of the iteration this same exact vanishing eliminates all sufficiently late oscillations on any fixed interval before $T_\infty$, which is how Proposition 8.1 obtains convergence of high derivatives.

e02.prop54.tail|TorusEuler.Paper.S5.rema.annotation: A slow label product has assigned level $i+j$, and a fast phase product has level $i+j-1$. Canceling all levels through $P$ leaves $i+j\ge P+1$ and $i+j\ge P+2$, respectively. The remaining linear terms are precisely the correction of $V_P$ and the label gradient of its pressure, which would be relayed to level $P+1$ (see Equation (5.38) for the quantitative remainder bound).

e02.prop54.tail|TorusEuler.hierarchyTail.annotation: The index square is filtered by $i+j-\mathrm{shift}>P$. Taking shift zero for label advection and one for phase advection gives the two thresholds in Equation (5.30). In the fast case the first index can start at two because $C_1=B_1=0$. The filtration is a finite-sum identity; the estimates for those products come later.

e02.prop54.outside-phase|TorusEuler.Hier.annotation: The twisted continuation is $F(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=F(t,a,s)$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^3$. Consequently $F(t,a+n,k_*\cdot(a+n))=F(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$. The phase independence of the tail near the cell faces allows this continuation without a jump in any derivative; its periodic mean products need no phase matching (see the proof of Lemma 5.7).

r2.prop54.divergence-proof|TorusEuler.Pa.annotation: The endpoint inverse writes $B=D_aX v$, with $v=z_t$ and $\operatorname{div}_a v=0$ (Theorem 4.2). Since the parent flow preserves volume, the Piola identity gives $\mathbf d\cdot B=\operatorname{div}_a v=0$. The mean has no phase derivative. This is how the label-space constraint of the inverse yields incompressibility in physical coordinates.

r2.prop54.level-cancellation|TorusEuler..annotation: The two equations in `IsExpansion` have separate right sides because the inverse for $B_p$ uses displacement endpoints while that for $V_p$ uses zero initial velocity. Adding them restores the full $-H_p$ and the supplementary source, along with the parent residual cancellation at level two. This is the termwise momentum cancellation used in Equation (5.29).

r2.prop54.switch-proof|TorusEuler.Paper..annotation: The cutoff $\widetilde\chi$ commutes with $C[\cdot]$ and with the slow pressure gradient, because they use only spatial derivatives. In the two linear momentum terms, differentiating the cutoff in time gives $\widetilde\chi'A_1$ and $\widetilde\chi'C[A_1]$. Their sum is the switch residual (3.8); the term $\widetilde\chi[(\partial_t+M)C[A_1]+\mathbf d\mathsf p[A_1]]$ is instead canceled at level two.

e02.prop54.surviving-levels|TorusEuler.h.annotation: The filtration groups each product by the integer $i+j-\mathrm{shift}$. Subtracting the sums for levels $2$ through $P$ leaves exactly the two tails in Equation (5.30). This applies to arbitrary summands; the expansion equations identify the terms to subtract.

e02.lemma55.completion|TorusEuler.Paper..annotation: The estimate uses the normalized covector, its normalized reciprocal squared length, and the inverse deformation in the slow curl. Their scaled derivatives are controlled by Equation (5.8). The weight $\gamma^{-1}$ commutes with the spatial operators, so the same bound holds even during the small-amplitude part of the launch interval.

e02.lemma55.momentum-hypothesis|TorusEul.annotation: Use the momentum equation to eliminate $V_t$ before estimating $Q_t$. The potentially fast pressure term disappears since $\kappa\times(\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p)=0$. The remaining label pressure gradient is estimated separately from Equation (5.16); its centered primitive also has the factor $|\kappa|^{-1}$. The relay thus needs $f$ at one higher spatial order, with no time derivative of $f$.

e02.lemma55.unswitched|TorusEuler.Paper..annotation: At level two use $A_1$ in Equation (5.32), which solves the homogeneous equation on $[t_0,T]$. Using $V_1=\widetilde\chi A_1$ would instead introduce the forcing $\widetilde\chi'A_1$. Those switch derivatives belong to $R_{\widetilde\chi}$, leaving the homogeneous relay multiplied by $\widetilde\chi$ in $H_2$.

e02.lemma55.potential-frequency|TorusEul.annotation: Set $k=\kappa/\lambda$. Then $Q[V]=-\lambda^{-1}(k/|k|^2)\times\partial_s^{-1}V$, because $k$ is independent of $s$. The normalized coefficient $k/|k|^2$ has scaled label norms controlled by Equation (5.8); differentiation of it does not cost an additional power of $\lambda$. The slow curl of this expression retains the same prefactor.

e02.lemma55.no-time-derivatives|TorusEul.annotation: In Equation (5.33) the forcing is evaluated at the current time. For the relay from $V_p$, the contribution of the newly solved mean enters through $f_p^S$ and hence algebraically through $B_p$. This avoids the need to estimate $\partial_t B_p$ using the endpoint equation. The smoothness of the profiles justifies differentiation; the quantitative induction needs only the label and phase norms.

e02.thm56.level-bounds|TorusEuler.hierar.annotation: The mean exponent is the sum of the two ordinary velocity exponents on $i+j=p$. In particular at level two the mean source has the scale of the square of the leading velocity, $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Averaging the fast product would give a worse power without Equation (5.42), which transfers its phase derivative to the slow divergence of the preceding generator. The mean inverse preserves the resulting frequency power up to parent factors.

r2.thm56.parent-exponent|TorusEuler.Pape.annotation: For the numerical recurrence take $L$ to bound each primitive coefficient or inverse cost. Starting with the parent-free transverse source, the inverse gives $V_i$ a factor $L$, and the completion can cost $L^2$. A slow product of two such blocks, including its advection estimate, costs at most $L^5$. The mean inverse gives $L^6$; the smallness condition absorbs this factor before the new mean is used in Equation (5.28). This counts losses along the current level, not along all previous levels.

r2.thm56.level-block-definitions|TorusEu.annotation: At fixed level $i$, $Z_i$ has full divergence $\mathbf d\cdot V_i-\mathbf d\cdot V_{i-1}$. This is generally nonzero. The size blocks are chosen to estimate products; the solenoidal grouping instead pairs $V_i$ with $C_{i+1}$. The difference between these two groupings is essential in Equation (5.42), where the divergence of $V_{i-1}$ replaces phase differentiation of $C_i$.

e02.thm56.fast-mean-integration|TorusEul.annotation: Integrate in the independent phase at fixed $(t,a)$: $\langle(C_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_j\rangle_s=-\langle\partial_s(C_i\cdot\kappa)Y_j\rangle_s$. By Equation (3.6), $\partial_s(C_i\cdot\kappa)=-\mathbf d\cdot V_{i-1}$. Thus the averaged interaction contains a label derivative of $V_{i-1}$ and no fast derivative. Its indices now sum to $(i-1)+j=p$, rather than $i+j=p+1$. In particular at $p=2$ it has two leading-wave factors, just like the slow product.

e01.correction.approximate-velocity|Toru.annotation: The contribution of level one is the completed primary field $\widetilde\chi(A_1+C[A_1])^\natural$. Keeping it separate from the higher oscillatory levels and the mean permits the central derivative of $A_1^\natural$ to be read as $\mathbf a\otimes\kappa$. The divergence completion and all the other terms contribute to the error in Equation (5.50).

euler02.approximate.fields|TorusEuler.Hi.annotation:
There are two different pressure normalizations. Zero phase mean fixes the primitive of a phase pressure before evaluation; zero spatial mean fixes the additive constant of the Poisson pressure. Graph evaluation need not preserve the first mean as the second. More importantly, for $u=V+v_\Lambda$, $\Delta(p-\Pi)=-\operatorname{div}R_V-\operatorname{tr}(
abla v_\Lambda
abla V+
abla u
abla v_\Lambda)$. Thus changing to the Poisson pressure is not merely a normalization by a constant; both sources in this equation must be estimated (see the proof of Proposition 5.11).

euler02.approximate.step-constant|TorusE.annotation: In step $j$, $\mathsf D=\lambda_{j-1}^9$ and $\Gamma_P\le\mathcal B(q_{j+1})\le\lambda_{j-1}$. Hence $C_{\rm step}\le\lambda_{j-1}^{9b+1}\le\lambda_{j-1}^{10b}$. In terms of the new frequency this is at most $\lambda_j^{10b/K_j}$, which is the parent loss to be absorbed in Equation (7.8).

euler02.approximate.graph-mean|TorusEule.annotation: For the mean, $\widetilde{\mathbf d}f=\mathbf df$; all successive derivatives remain phase independent since the coframe has no $s$ dependence. Thus each derivative costs only a power of the parent bound, regardless of the new carrier. This accounts for the common frequency power $\lambda^{-5/2}$ at all orders of the mean in Equation (5.48).

euler02.approximate.holder-from-jets|Tor.annotation: For $d=|x-y|>0$, let $B_j,B_{j+1}$ bound the derivatives of orders $j,j+1$. The difference of the order-$j$ derivatives is at most $\min(2B_j,B_{j+1}d)\le\sqrt{2B_jB_{j+1}d}$. Dividing by $\sqrt d$ gives the half-Hölder seminorm. Taking $B_j,B_{j+1}\le B$ gives the linked bound $3(m+1)B$ on the sum of the supremum norms and seminorms through $m$. This explains the one extra ordinary derivative used in Equation (5.45).

r5-B-depth-remainder|TorusEuler.Paper.S5.annotation: After inserting $P=6K_{j+1}$, the hierarchy contribution and the switched contribution each decay like $\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ before their prefactors. Item 4 of the proof of Theorem 7.1 obtains $2\lambda^{2+1/16}\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-7/2}$. This is an estimate on $R_V$ before the projection and Fourier correction; the induction needs a bound on $R_j$ after them. The spare half-power of $\lambda_{j+1}$ allows those constants to be absorbed into (T2).

euler02.approximate.regularity|TorusEule.annotation: The matrix and coframe in the hierarchy are those of the actual flow of $U$, namely $M=\nabla U\circ X$ and $(D_aX)^{-T}$. Although the leading wave is chosen using the equations at the center, graph evaluation uses the full spatially varying coefficients. Consequently there is no additional error from replacing the parent by its linearization in Equation (5.46).

euler02.approximate.physical-estimates|T.annotation: The high-order bound on the oscillation is used in the opposite way from (5.47): it need not be small, since it is multiplied by a Fourier-tail factor. At the chosen depth item 4 of the proof of Theorem 7.1 gives $1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}}\le3\lambda^{2(P+1)}$. In (5.55) the cutoff $\Lambda=\lambda^5$ then gives $9\lambda^{5(2-P)+4(P+1)}=9\lambda^{14-P}$. With this bound, a cutoff at $\lambda^4$ would not yield decay with $P$. The extra power makes increasing the depth effective even after squaring the full velocity norm.

euler02.approximate.parent-cancellation|.annotation: Explicitly, $(R_U\circ X)^\natural(t,x)=R_U(t,X(t,A(t,x)))=R_U(t,x)$. The level-two mean source in (5.27) contains its negative, so this cancellation also removes the phase-independent part of the old defect. The new residual is not the sum of the old residual and the hierarchy remainder.

In label coordinates the parent source in the momentum equation is $R_U(t,X(t,a))$, independent of $s$. The hierarchy has been constructed with its negative as the level-two mean source. At the physical point $x=X(t,a)$ the two terms are literally equal with opposite signs; no estimate on $\|R_U\|$ is needed for their cancellation in Equation (5.46).

euler02.pressure-flow.pressure-upper|Tor.annotation: The center coupling $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a$ remains positive on the chosen label support by Equation (5.19). This extension of the sign, rather than positivity only at $a=0$, is needed for the Hessian bound on the whole torus. The time cutoff is nonnegative, and outside the active support the primary pressure coefficient is zero.

euler02.pressure-flow.mean-hessian|Torus.annotation: `MeanHessianClaim` is the norm estimate for the sum of the phase-independent pressures. Since the mean velocity and source in its Poisson equation are phase independent, their conversion to physical $C^{1,1/2}$ norms costs powers of $\mathsf D$ but no $\lambda^{3/2}$ factor. This leaves the rate $\lambda^{-5/2}$ from Equation (5.37).

euler02.pressure-flow.center-smallness|T.annotation: The intermediate estimate is $C_{2,P}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/12}$. Since $C_{2,P}\mathsf D^C\le C_{\rm step}$, the factor $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}$ in Equation (5.43) is at most one. This leaves $\lambda^{-1/3}$, a bound with no parent-dependent prefactor, as required for the next frame comparison.

euler02.pressure-flow.deformation|TorusE.annotation: The selected wave and its hierarchy are fixed before the perturbation $v$ is specified. The bound holds for every admissible small solenoidal $v$, in particular the truncation tail chosen later, estimated in Equation (5.56). This order of quantifiers is needed to pass from the constructed expansion to its truncated successor.

euler02.truncation.residual-definition|T.annotation: The cutoff does not preserve the momentum equation, even when $R_V=0$: $u\otimes u$ need not equal $S_\Lambda(V\otimes V)$. The actual new defect in `residual` is the one for the recovered pressure. By Equation (5.58) its two sources are the projected filtered defect $\mathbb P S_\Lambda R_V$ and the projected divergence of this tensor difference.

euler-r2.truncation.quadratic-tensor-cos.annotation: All three tensors in Equation (5.58) need a bound of order two, but only one factor in each mixed product needs to be small. The tail $v_\Lambda$ gives $\Lambda^{2-P}\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}}$, and $u$ and $V$ are bounded by $C\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}}$. For the last tensor apply the tail estimate directly to $V\otimes V$, whose high norm is quadratic in the same norm of $V$. Thus there is one tail factor, not two, in the common budget.

euler02.truncation.holder-product|TorusE.annotation: At order two the first mixed tensor in Equation (5.58) is bounded by $C\|v_\Lambda\|_{C^{2,1/2}}\|u\|_{C^{2,1/2}}$. Uniform boundedness of $S_\Lambda$ controls the second factor by the norm of $V$. The other mixed tensor has the analogous bound. One tail factor is sufficient; neither $u$ nor $V$ is required to be small in that norm.

euler02.truncation.final-upper-bound|Tor.annotation: For the next endpoint inverse (Theorem 4.2), write $\mu=\lambda_{j-1}$ and $\lambda=\lambda_j$. The initial shear has constant pressure, and the upper bounds on subsequent pressure increments sum to at most $2/N$. The parent residual has band $4\mu^5$ and norm at most $\lambda^{-3}$; Bernstein gives $\|\nabla R_U\|_\infty\le C\mu^5\lambda^{-3}$. Consequently $D^2p_U-\nabla R_U\le(2/N+C\mu^5\lambda^{-3})I\le I$ for large $N$, as required by the next mean inverse (Theorem 4.2).

e03-s6-fixed-second-coordinate|TorusEule.annotation: The equation for the second particle coordinate is $\dot X_{0,2}=0$. Hence the velocity of each particle remains its initial velocity, and integration gives the affine-in-time trajectory in Equation (6.2).

e03-s6-lemma61-strength|TorusEuler.Paper.annotation: At zero the leading velocity gradient has size $\lambda|\mathbf a(0,0)|$, since $F_h'(0)=1$. In contrast, the leading velocity has size at most $C\lambda^{-3/4}h=C\lambda^{-5/4}$. The steep slope of $F_h$ (Lemma 3.1) thus produces a shear of order $\lambda^{1/4}$ from a small velocity increment.

e03-s6-positive-first-coupling|TorusEule.annotation: The loss from $2\pi$ is at most $2t|B_\rho|^2\le |B_\rho|/4\le\pi$. The resulting $\nu\ge\pi$ is stronger than the $\mathsf D^{-1}$ needed in Equation (5.5).

e03-s6-growing-initial-direction|TorusEu.annotation: In the strong-shear system at $\tau=0$, $\alpha_1'=-\alpha_2$ and $\alpha_2'=-\alpha_1$. The vector $(-1,1)$ belongs to the growing eigendirection. Undoing the scaling in Equation (2.3) gives $-E_1/S+E_2$, which is perpendicular to the chosen launch normal $E_3$.

r2-s6-reference-turn|TorusEuler.MovingWa.annotation: The reference turning time is at least $2/\varepsilon$, whereas the cutoff has completed by normalized time one. A crossing in the stated bracket therefore gives both the target coupling ratio and the full preceding shear for the next step. Its strength is estimated by Equation (2.23), which uses the product of the amplitude and the now longer wave vector.

r2-s7-actual-oscillation|TorusEuler.Pape.annotation: The equality in the step data is with the oscillation of the hierarchy *before* the Fourier cutoff. The support and zero-data assertions follow at the profile level. Applying the multiplier to the oscillation itself would in general destroy its spatial localization (used in the proof of Proposition 8.4), even though it would preserve zero time slices.

e03-s7-T1|TorusEuler.paperTheorem71|1.annotation: The band $|\xi|\le2\Lambda_j$ is imposed on the truncated velocity $U_j$. It is unrelated to an integer constraint on the central covector of a wave. At the next step it allows arbitrary fixed spatial derivatives of the parent to be estimated by Bernstein (B.1) from $\|U_j\|_\infty$, without differentiating the hierarchy that produced it.

e03-s7-T4-splitting|TorusEuler.paperTheo.annotation: The full rank-one term has norm $\sigma_j$ at the crossing and becomes the preceding shear of Equation (6.5). It is not enough to approximate that matrix to a small relative error: the scaled amplitude equation multiplies the central error by $S/r=1/(2\nu)$, not by $1/\sigma$. The absolute tolerance $\lambda_j^{-1/4}$ therefore keeps the comparison error small even when the leading matrix grows without bound.

e03-s7-oscillation-support|TorusEuler.Pa.annotation: Fourier truncation is nonlocal in space. The compact support retained by the finite oscillatory profiles is therefore assigned to their physical evaluation $O_j$ before truncation. The difference produced by the multiplier is included with the mean in the remainder of Equation (7.4).

e03-s7-inactive-oscillation|TorusEuler.P.annotation: For $j\ge2$, $O_j(0)=0$. The phase-independent correction is solved with zero displacement at both ends (Section 4.1), which is not zero velocity at both ends. Its initial value can therefore change $U_j(0)$; (7.4) makes these changes, including the Fourier errors, summable at every fixed spatial order.

e03-s7-low-gradient|TorusEuler.exists_pa.annotation: The spatial Bernstein bound costs one power of $\Lambda_j=\lambda_j^5$ and gives $C\lambda_j^6$ for the gradient. To estimate $\partial_t\nabla U_j$, take one spatial derivative in Equation (7.5). The quadratic term now contains two derivatives and the Leray projection is bounded in $C^{0,1/2}$; using a third ordinary derivative to control this Hölder norm costs $C\Lambda_j^3\lambda_j^2=C\lambda_j^{17}$. Together with the small differentiated residual this fits $\lambda_j^{18}$. The Hölder step avoids using an $L^\infty$ operator bound for the projection.

e03-s7-half-length-decay|TorusEuler.freq.annotation: By Equation (1.15), $\tau_j\le\mu^{-1/8}(\log\mu)^6\le\mu^{-1/16}$ for large $N$. At $j+1$ this gives $4\tau_{j+1}\le4\lambda_j^{-1/16}\le4\mu^{-1/4}\le\mu^{-1/8}\le\tau_j$. The last inequality uses $L_{j+1}\ge1$. Both estimates are uniform because $\mu\ge N$.

e03-s7-growth-rate|TorusEuler.activation.annotation: The square root in $r=\sqrt{2\sigma\nu}$ turns the strength bounds at the preceding crossing into $c\mu^{1/8}\le r\le C\mu^{1/8}L_j$. Consequently $2r\tau_j$ is between $2cL_{j+1}^3$ and $CL_jL_{j+1}^3\le CL_{j+1}^4$. The lower estimate allows the required crossing, and the upper one limits the polynomial loss in Equation (2.7).

e03-s7-switch-residual|TorusEuler.exists.annotation: The derivative is confined to the first normalized unit. There $\gamma\le e^{3-L_j}$ and $|\widetilde\chi'|\le Cr$, so $\|\widetilde\chi'\gamma\|_\infty\le Ce^3\mu^{1/8}L_j\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}\le\mu\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. The last inequality follows from Equation (1.15), uniformly in $j$. Wave one contributes no switching residual.

r2-s7-new-truncation|TorusEuler.Paper.Th.annotation: The velocity $V$ is the exactly divergence-free field obtained from the finite expansion. The new parent is $U_j=S_{\Lambda_j}V$, and its pressure is computed afresh from $\Delta\pi_j=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla U_j)^2)$. If $v_\Lambda=U_j-V$, then $U_j-U_{j-1}=O_j+\bar W^\natural+v_\Lambda$. The last two terms, rather than the oscillation itself, will have small high-order norms. This is the decomposition used in Equation (7.4).

e03-s8-initial-smooth|TorusEuler.PaperLi.annotation: The uniform limit on the closed slab defines both $w(0)$ and $w(T_\infty)$. The additional preactivation vanishing at $t=0$ upgrades the first of these limits to every fixed spatial order. At the terminal time the corresponding upgrade from Equation (7.4) is local, on compact sets separated from the shrinking supports of the oscillations.

e03-s8-initial-smooth|TorusEuler.Paper.p.annotation: The approximations are not exact Euler evolutions from $U_j(0)$, so continuity of the Euler solution map on its own would not identify their limit. Instead Equation (7.5) provides an integrated equation with an explicit residual tending to zero. The limit of the initial slices is then the datum of the exact equation obtained from that identity.

e03-s7-all-orders|TorusEuler.frequencySc.annotation: Fix $m$ first. Once $q_j\ge m$, all subsequent remainders in Equation (7.4) are bounded in $C_tC^{m,1/2}$ by $\lambda_j^{-1}$. Choosing a later index so that $t_j\ge T$ gives the same estimate for the full increments on $[0,T]$ when $T<T_\infty$.

e03-s8-bounded-velocity|TorusEuler.Paper.annotation: The global velocity estimate involves no sum of gradients. At the level of Equation (5.44), the oscillation has size $\lambda_j^{-5/4}$ and a first derivative bounded by $\lambda_j^{1/4}$, up to parent powers. The frequency grows much faster than the parent factors. This explains how the former estimate gives summability while the central derivative, whose lower bound requires the separate projection argument, can grow without bound.

e03-s8-rank-one|TorusEuler.coordinateCur.annotation: For the linear field $v(x)=\mathbf a(\kappa\cdot x)$, the gradient is $\mathbf a\otimes\kappa$ and $\operatorname{curl}v=\nabla(\kappa\cdot x)\times\mathbf a=\kappa\times\mathbf a$. This fixes the sign in Equation (8.1); the reverse cross product would give the opposite surviving component.

r2-s8-geometry-before-projection|TorusEu.annotation: In item 2 of the proof of Theorem 7.1 the rate is $r\le C\mu^{1/8}L_j$, where $\mu=\lambda_{j-1}$, and the reserved time is $S_j-t_j=2\mu^{-1/8}L_{j+1}^3$. Their product is at most $CL_jL_{j+1}^3\le CL_{j+1}^4$. The wave-vector length bound is quadratic in this normalized time, giving the $L_{j+1}^8$ loss in the projection. The frequency power $\mu^{1/8}$ cancels when computing the normalized window.

e03-s8-maximal-and-integrals|TorusEuler..annotation: For a nonnegative function, even a limit to infinity at a finite endpoint does not imply an infinite integral. Here the additional information is the time spent at each vorticity scale (see Section 8.4): for $\mu=\lambda_{j-1}$ the lower bound is $c\mu^{1/8}$ on an interval of length at least $cL_j\mu^{-1/8}$. The product grows like $L_j$, so the formal proof can bound the full integral below by the integral on a single sufficiently late interval. The upper bounds on the durations used to prove finite accumulation cannot serve this purpose.

e03-s8-off-origin|TorusEuler.PaperTermin.annotation: The velocity traces on different compact sets are restrictions of the same globally continuous $w(T_\infty)$. The time-derivative traces agree on overlaps by uniqueness of their order-zero limits. Thus the conclusion gives well-defined spatial fields on the punctured torus for velocity and its first time derivative, but not a limit of every time derivative. The latter needs the extra mixed-derivative estimates in the auxiliary note (Lemma 1.2).

e03-s8-shrinking-support|TorusEuler.indu.annotation: Put $d=\operatorname{dist}_{\mathbb T^3}(K,0)>0$. For late $j$, the ball of radius $\lambda_{j-1}^{-1}<d/2$ misses the open $d/2$ neighborhood of $K$, uniformly in time. On that neighborhood the entire increment equals $U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j$. This is why one can apply Equation (7.4) to its derivatives there even though the Fourier-truncated increment is not itself supported in the ball.

e03-r2-appa-symmetry|TorusEuler.Paper.St.annotation: For the parent flow these symmetries follow from $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Skew-symmetry gives $\Omega w\cdot w=0$, but not $\Omega z_t\cdot z=0$. In the path problem the latter term represents the effect of the pulled-back vorticity on a displacement, and must be included in Equation (A.2).

e03-appa-forcing-continuity|TorusEuler.P.annotation: On the normalized interval the inclusion $C_tC_a^{0,1/2}\hookrightarrow C_a^{0,1/2}(L_t^2)$ has norm at most one: apply $\|h\|_{L_t^2}\le\sup_t|h(t)|$ to the values and to each difference of label paths. Continuity of $L(t)$ in the stronger norm is used when the right-hand side of Equation (A.9) is formed.

e03-appa-a1-equation-and-traces|TorusEul.annotation: The quantity in `paperMeanIntegratedMomentum` is $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L$. Its solenoidal part is constant in time; its gradient part need not be. For a force source $L=-Jg$, the label pressure in the differential equation (4.11) is $\mathsf q=-\phi_t$, not $\phi$ itself: differentiation removes the integration constant and gives $Kv_t+(K_t-\Omega)v+\nabla_a\mathsf q=g$.

e03-appa-a2-base-isomorphism|TorusEuler..annotation: By Equation (A.5), $\mathcal RBv=0$ implies $v=0$. The range is also closed, since the estimate makes preimages of a Cauchy sequence of outputs Cauchy in the projected Hölder space. To prove that all projected data lie in the range, the paper starts with $B=I$, where this is true, and preserves surjectivity by continuation. `Paper.lemma_A_2` supplies the proved isomorphism in both the spatial and the path-valued cases.

e03-appa-a2-higher-isomorphism|TorusEule.annotation: In the higher-order clause of `FreezingConclusion` the map is the same equivalence $e$ as in Equation (A.5), with $v$ of higher regularity exactly when $ev$ has higher regularity. Bounds for both $\|ev\|_{C^{k,1/2}}$ and $\|v\|_{C^{k,1/2}}$ give continuity in the higher norm. This is how the formal statement expresses an isomorphism in that norm.

e03-appa-frozen-multiplier-bound|TorusEu.annotation: Both symbols $A_0^{-1}$ and $A_0^{-1}r$ give order-zero operators with the same type of half-Hölder bound. The first acts on $f$ in Equation (A.7); the second takes the unprojected coefficient errors as its inputs. The formal estimate takes $C_0\le C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B_0\|)^{11}$, which controls the dependence on $B_0$ in the subsequent choice of the cutoff radius.

e03-appb-kernel-derivative-scale|TorusEu.annotation: The identity leaves the factor $(4\Lambda)^{|\beta|}$ when derivatives are moved to the kernel of the reproducing cutoff. Summing these bounds gives Equation (B.1), absorbing $4^{|\beta|}$ in $C_m$. The linked full lemma gives Bernstein, rather than stating the kernel identity separately.

e03-appd-exact-order-norm|TorusEuler.app.annotation: Here $|c|_m$ is a sum over derivatives of exact order $m$. In particular $|c|_0$ need not be small when the positive-order terms of the finite norm are small. This distinction is used in Equation (D.7), which involves only $m\ge1$.

e03-appd-radius-coeff|TorusEuler.Paper.S.annotation: Lemma D.2(c) is stronger than boundedness of the scaled coefficient norm: for $m\ge1$ it retains $\ell_*^m|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{2a}\ell_*$ with integer $a$ in Lean. The zero-order term has size $C_0\mathsf D^a$ and is not part of the smallness condition. If an exponent is enlarged after multiplication or inversion, impose the radius restriction with the new exponent.

e03-appd-lifting-equation|TorusEuler.Pap.annotation: For the mean the constraint belongs to the displacement $z$, with $z(0)=z(T)=0$ and $v=z_t$. The integrated equation contains $Kv$ and the time integral of $\Omega v$, modulo a label gradient. Taking a label derivative preserves the constraints and produces the same integrated equation for the differentiated unknown, with a new forcing. The inverse from the preceding section supplies existence; Lemma D.3 estimates such solutions.

e03-r2-appd-constraint-subspace|TorusEul.annotation: The differentiation must preserve the space on which the zero-order inverse is available. In the mean problem, label derivatives preserve both the divergence constraint and the endpoint values of the displacement. In the transverse problem this is why one works in fixed coordinates as in Equation (5.18): direct differentiation of $\kappa\cdot V=0$ introduces the inhomogeneous constraint $\kappa\cdot\partial_{a_i}V=-(\partial_{a_i}\kappa)\cdot V$.

adapted.E4-D-05.1|TorusEuler.Paper.lemma.annotation: Separate the term in which all derivatives hit the unknown from those in which at least one hits a coefficient. The former belongs to the original inverse equation; the latter have the radius gain from Lemma D.2(c). In the Hölder case (D.2) uses half of that gain, leaving $\ell_*^{1/2}$. Choose the radius once to absorb the polynomial inverse cost; Lemma D.3 then gives the desired estimate without an additional parent power at each derivative order.

c8-auxiliary-abstract-extension|TorusEul.annotation: The main paper (Proposition M.8.4) obtains a limit for $\partial_tu$ away from the origin using the projected equation: the local stress converges in a Hölder norm and the distant stress is handled by the smooth pressure kernel off the diagonal. This does not directly iterate, since higher time derivatives of the distant stress have not been controlled. The auxiliary note obtains these derivatives by estimating the stage increments instead. Its conclusion concerns the velocity, not an Euler solution continued through the singular time.

e03-aux-time-display|TorusEuler.Paper.Au.annotation: This condition combines the two numerical bounds through order $q$ at a single stage with continuity in the uniform spatial norm. The exponent is a nonnegative integer. Lemma 1.3 of the auxiliary note additionally proves that some such exponent works from a sufficiently late index onward.

e03-aux-base-mixed|TorusEuler.InductiveE.annotation: At time order zero the mixed correction is the second estimate of (M.7.4). For fixed $m$, the inequality holds when $q_j\ge m$, which eventually follows from order growth. The linked result supplies the numerical Hölder bound; continuity of the correction curve is separate.

e03-aux-fixed-label-phase|TorusEuler.Hie.annotation: The independent phase $s$ is held fixed along with $a$. On a parent trajectory $x=X(t,a)$ the physical evaluation has phase $k_*\cdot a$, independent of time. Thus profile time differentiation corresponds to the material derivative $D_t$ (see Equation (M.3.1)), not the Eulerian derivative $\partial_t$. The transport term is restored in the later graph estimate.

e03-r2-aux-mean-time-gain-display|TorusE.annotation: The integrated endpoint inverse first bounds the actual $v=z_t$; it determines its initial trace from the two conditions on $z$. The fixed-time inverse of $\mathbb P(K(t)\cdot)$ then bounds each higher time derivative from the differentiated strong equation, using (M.D.3) in Hölder norms. This gives (2.3), with one extra label derivative on the source but one fewer time derivative. Lean chooses the minimum radius exponent before the time order (its index $q$ on the right corresponds to $q+1$ on the left), so the construction need not be changed for higher time orders.

e03-r2-aux-mean-source-order|TorusEuler..annotation: The hierarchy uses the mean-source norm at time order $q-1$ and the mean-velocity norm at order $q$. The oscillatory sources and their velocity and pressure solutions all use order $q$. This particular allocation allows the mean source in (M.5.27) to contain $R_U\circ X$ at level two without asking for the unavailable $q$th derivative of the old residual.

e03-r2-aux-tail-depth-identity|TorusEule.annotation: The remainder at depth $P$ has the factor $\lambda^{-2P/3}=\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ because $P=6K_{j+1}$. The activation error (M.3.8) has no such depth factor. It is supported only during the initial switch, when the seed amplitude is at most $Ce^{-L_j}=C\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. This is the separate reason both terms of the residual have the same next-frequency decay after graph conversion.

e03-aux-cutoff-commutation|TorusEuler.Tr.annotation: At step $j$ the operator $S_{\Lambda_j}$ is fixed throughout the slab. Therefore $\partial_t^q(S_{\Lambda_j}-\operatorname{Id})V=(S_{\Lambda_j}-\operatorname{Id})\partial_t^qV$. This permits direct application of (M.B.2) to each time jet of the uncut approximation; no derivative of the symbol or scale appears.

e03-aux-add-half-bounds|TorusEuler.Trunc.annotation: Both terms in the exact correction identity are estimated in the same mixed norm: the mean by (2.4), without any fast phase cost, and the Fourier tail by (M.B.2) applied to the time jet. Their bounds are each $\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$. Thus the estimate for the correction is global even though the oscillation it excludes is localized. Norm continuity on the closed slab is obtained separately.

e03-r2-aux-cutoff-residual-identity|Toru.annotation: Write $v=U_j-V$. Because time differentiation commutes with $S$, subtracting the cut and uncut projected equations, as in (M.5.58), leaves $SR_V$ and the projected divergence of $v\otimes U_j+V\otimes v+(\operatorname{Id}-S)(V\otimes V)$. Each of the three stress terms contains a cutoff tail. For the projected divergence in $C^{1,1/2}$ estimate the tensors in $C^{2,1/2}$; time differentiation distributes over the factors without removing the tail.

e03-aux-oscillations-leave-compact|Torus.annotation: Let $d=\operatorname{dist}(K,0)>0$ on the torus. Once the support radius of $O_j$ is less than $d/2$, the oscillation is identically zero on the open $d/2$-neighborhood of $K$ throughout the slab. On the periodic lift the separation is from the entire integer lattice. Consequently every mixed derivative of the late oscillations vanishes there. The increment bound (1.2) for the remaining terms is global; only the starting index and the early finite sum can depend on $d$.

e01.abstract.bounded-velocity|TorusEuler.annotation: At order zero, the new wave and the rest of the stage increment each contribute at most $\lambda_j^{-1}$ to the velocity increment (see Equation (7.4)). The sum of these bounds is finite, giving one speed bound for every $t<T_*$. Forming the curl differentiates the waves, so the same estimate cannot be applied to the curl.

e01.abstract.central-vorticity|TorusEule.annotation: The lower bound has to hold between every pair of sufficiently late launches. Projecting the central curl onto the newest wave vector kills that wave’s own leading contribution $k\times a$. The preceding wave supplies a positive component in this direction that dominates the older flow and the errors. (The two projections are in Equation (8.1).) The intervals cover a full left neighborhood of $T_*$, so the lower bound holds at all sufficiently late times.

e01.abstract.off-origin|TorusEuler.Euler.annotation: On a compact set away from the origin, the late oscillations disappear from the local velocity estimates because their supports shrink. For $\partial_tu$, the pressure still feels the flow near the origin. Its kernel is smooth across the positive distance to the compact set, so uniform convergence of the velocity on the torus suffices for the distant contribution (see the proof of Proposition 8.4).

r5-root-theorem11-complete|TorusEuler.Pa.annotation: The proof applies Proposition 8.1 to the constructed stage sequence at its accumulation time $T_\infty$. This gives the datum $u(0)$ and the Euler flow on $[0,T_\infty)$. Proposition 8.2 gives Equation (1.3), Corollary 8.3 identifies $T_*=T_\infty$ and proves Equation (1.2), and Proposition 8.4 supplies the two compact-set limits. Each step uses the same $u$.

r5-root-theorem11-complete|TorusEuler.Is.annotation: A continuation is a smooth Euler velocity on $[0,S)$ with $S>T_*$ that agrees with $u$ for all $t<T_*$. Its curl at the origin would be continuous on the compact interval $[0,T_*]$ and therefore bounded there. The divergence in Equation (1.3) rules out every such continuation.

r5-root-theorem11-complete|TorusEuler.Eu.annotation: The witness asks both for pointwise curl divergence at the origin and for divergence of the time integral of its spatial supremum. The paper obtains the integral conclusion from the continuation criterion (see the proof of Corollary 8.3). The Lean proof obtains it directly by multiplying a lower bound on the curl between launches by a lower bound on each late interval’s duration. The gradient integral then follows from $\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_\infty\le C\|\nabla u\|_\infty$.

e01.remark.smooth-extension|TorusEuler.P.annotation: The extension has to be smooth jointly in time and space near the terminal slice, so its mixed derivatives of every fixed order must reach $T_*$. The result in Theorem 1.1 supplies spatial limits for $u$ and $\partial_tu$. The stronger choice in Remark 1.2 adds time-derivative estimates before extending the field across the slice.

r2a1.intro.smooth-extension-proof-route|.annotation: In the auxiliary note, the threshold $\mathcal B$ is chosen to absorb constants in the estimates for time derivatives as well as spatial ones. The mixed-derivative tails then converge up to $T_*$ on compact sets away from the origin, where the late waves vanish. The checked proof obtains those bounds for a particular scheduled construction and uses its smooth extension to prove the existential claim in Remark 1.2.

e01.intro.approximate-sequence|TorusEule.annotation: The construction chooses the threshold function before choosing the starting frequency $N$. For each sufficiently large $N$, the recursion fixes a sequence of orders and frequencies, and the construction supplies the corresponding stages on a common time slab (see Theorem 7.1). The orders tend to infinity, so any fixed derivative order can eventually be controlled along that sequence.

r2a1.intro.wave.velocity|TorusEuler.Pape.annotation: The wave derivative sends $v$ to $F'(k\cdot x)(k\cdot v)\mathbf a$. Taking its trace gives $F'(k\cdot x)(k\cdot\mathbf a)$, and feeding in $w$ gives $F'(k\cdot x)F(k\cdot x)(k\cdot\mathbf a)\mathbf a$. Thus one perpendicularity condition removes both the wave divergence and its quadratic self-interaction. The exact-wave theorem uses the two ODEs in Equation (1.4) for the remaining terms.

intro.preceding-frame|TorusEuler.MovingW.annotation: The strength $\sigma$ is the magnitude of both the rank-one gradient (in operator norm) and the vorticity of the preceding wave at the origin. Here it is a function of time; in Section 2.2.1 it is denoted by $\sigma_p(t)$, and $\sigma=\sigma_p(t_0)$ is frozen at launch. The latter is `initialStrength` in Lean.

intro-amplification-polarization|TorusEu.annotation:
At launch $a_3=0$ and pressure acts only along $E_3$. The frozen two-component system has growing rate $g=\sqrt{2
u(\sigma-
u)}$ and ratio $a_1/a_2=-2
u/g=-S^{-1}(1-1/(2S^2))^{-1/2}$, where $S=\sqrt{\sigma/(2
u)}$. Taking just $-S^{-1}$ makes the scaled initial data exactly $(-1,1)$ in Equation (2.3); the discarded relative correction is $O(S^{-2})$.

r2a1.intro.strong-shear-factor|TorusEule.annotation: The vanishing of the driving coefficient is not the vanishing of the growth rate. Put $s=\cos\varphi$. Eliminating $\alpha_1$ in Equation (2.5) gives $(s^{-2}a_{\rm ref}')'=(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)a_{\rm ref}$. Since $a_{\rm ref}>0$ and $a_{\rm ref}'(0)=1$, the weighted derivative is still positive when $\varepsilon\tan\varphi=1$. Only afterwards does it decrease to zero, at the maximum located by Lemma 2.5.

intro-amplification-new-couplings|TorusE.annotation: The older gradient here is the one seen by the present wave (called $M$ in Section 2.2). Its coupling entries in the new frame are unchanged by adding $\mathbf a\otimes k$, since $(\mathbf a\otimes k)E_{2,+}=0$. In the periodic construction the actual next parent also has a central correction error; that error must be estimated separately, rather than included in the prescribed ratio.

intro-amplification-cancellation|TorusEu.annotation: The cancellation in the third coupling is a consequence of the amplitude direction as well as the normal. In the notation of Equation (2.13), put $s=\cos\varphi$ and $u=\varepsilon\tau\sin\varphi/2$, so the logarithmic amplitude rate satisfies $Y/s=1+e-u$. The second expression for the reference couplings, divided by $s$, is $\varepsilon\tan\varphi-1+2(Y/s+u)^2-2u^2$. Since $2u^2=\varepsilon\tan\varphi\sin^2\varphi$, this reduces to $1+4e+2e^2+\varepsilon\sin\varphi\cos\varphi$. The remaining coefficient is close to one; estimating the original terms separately would lose the small factor $s$.

localized.intro.real-wave-vector|TorusEu.annotation: The condition $k_*\cdot n\in\mathbb Z$ for every lattice vector $n$ would be necessary for the phase modulo one to be well defined everywhere on the torus. Here we periodically extend the evaluated, supported potential instead. Its zero collar removes the need to match phases on opposite faces, leaving the direction of the wave vector free; its curl is then a smooth periodic solenoidal velocity. (For periodic extension, see the proof of Lemma 5.7.)

c8-endpoint-choice-introduction|TorusEul.annotation: In the scalar analogue $y''-m^2y=f$ of Equation (1.7), a constant force and zero initial position and velocity give $y=f(\cosh(mt)-1)/m^2$. If instead we choose $y'(0)=-(f/m)\tanh(mT/2)$, the solution has $y(0)=y(T)=0$ and $|y(t)|\le |f|/m^2$ on the entire interval. The choice of the initial velocity removes the large response; the problem below is to make such a choice with the incompressibility constraint.

e01.endpoint.first-variation-equation|To.annotation: The displacement variable of Section 4 has a direct interpretation. The relative map $X(t,\cdot)^{-1}\circ X_\delta(t,\cdot)$ is the identity at $\delta=0$, and its derivative in $\delta$ is $z=(D_aX)^{-1}\xi$. Its time derivative is $v=(D_aX)^{-1}(b\circ X)$ by Equation (1.5). Both maps preserve volume, so $z$ is divergence free in labels. These are the displacement and velocity stored in the smooth mean solution.

r2a1.intro.initial-displacement|TorusEul.annotation: The endpoint condition is on the position of each particle. Since $X_\delta(0,a)=a$ for every $\delta$, the initial displacement is zero independently of the choice of $b$. At either end, Equation (1.5) now gives $\xi_t=b\circ X$; the slopes at the two ends need not vanish. In particular $b(0)$ is available to enforce the terminal condition.

e01.endpoint.selected-initial-value|Toru.annotation: For two choices of initial velocity with the same force and zero terminal displacement, the difference solves Equation (1.7) with $f=0$ and both traces zero. The quadratic form in Equations (1.8)–(1.9) rules out a nonzero difference. This is injectivity of the linearized endpoint map; existence of the required initial value is the additional content of the inverse in Section 4.3.

e01.endpoint.linearized-euler|TorusEuler.annotation: At fixed label put $B=b\circ X$ and $M=(\nabla u)\circ X$. The linearized momentum equation becomes $B_t+MB+(\nabla q)\circ X=f\circ X$, with $B=\xi_t-M\xi$ from Equation (1.5). Substitution cancels the two terms containing $M\xi_t$ and leaves the Jacobi equation with coefficient $-(M_t+M^2)$. This is why a first-order equation for $b$ leads to a two-endpoint problem for $\xi$.

e01.endpoint.pressure-cancellation|Torus.annotation: Let $F=D_aX$. Since $F_t=MF$ and $\operatorname{tr} M=0$, Jacobi’s formula gives $(\det F)_t=0$ and $\det F=1$. This removes the change-of-variables factor in Equation (1.8). Vanishing of the pressure integral also uses the first-order constraint on $\xi\circ X^{-1}$.

e01.endpoint.coercivity|TorusEuler.endpo.annotation: If $H\le hI$ with $h\ge0$, Equation (1.8) gives the lower bound $(1-hT^2/2)\|\xi_t\|_2^2$. Thus it is the product of the upper curvature bound with the square of the interval length that matters for this estimate. With $h=1$ and $T\le1$ the loss is at most one half, regardless of the magnitude of negative eigenvalues.

The form in Equation (1.9) is written in the physical displacement. Appendix A solves instead for the label velocity $v=(D_aX)^{-1}(b\circ X)$, with $z=\int_0^t v$ and $\xi=D_aXz$. The identity (4.7) is what transfers the lower bound to the quadratic form of that operator. The linked lemma is this transfer for continuously differentiable paths; the $L^2$ version used in the inverse is obtained by density.

r2a1.intro.hessian-upper|TorusEuler.endp.annotation: The sign in the energy is $-\xi\cdot H\xi$. A negative eigenvalue therefore improves the lower bound, even if its magnitude is large. Later the wave pressure Hessian has leading term $-p_{\rm w}F_h'(s)k\otimes k$; for $p_{\rm w}>0$ only the shallow negative part of $F_h'$ produces positive curvature. This explains the asymmetric profile in Equation (1.10).

e01.endpoint.approximate-hessian|TorusEu.annotation: Write $B=b\circ X$. Combining $\xi_t=M\xi+B$ with $B_t=-MB-(\nabla q)\circ X+f\circ X$ gives $\xi_{tt}=(M_t+M^2)\xi-(\nabla q)\circ X+f\circ X$. Thus the coefficient of $\xi$ on the left of Equation (1.7) is $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)$ even without an exact Euler equation. Differentiating the parent's residual identity then gives Equation (4.3); a pressure Hessian alone would omit the residual gradient.

e01.endpoint.quantitative-inverse|TorusE.annotation: For a solution satisfying the two end conditions, Equations (1.8)–(1.9) and volume preservation give $\tfrac12\|\xi_t\|_2^2\le \|f\|_2\|\xi\|_2\le (T/\sqrt2)\|f\|_2\|\xi_t\|_2$. Hence $\|\xi_t\|_2\le\sqrt2T\|f\|_2$. This estimate cannot control a value of $\xi_t$ at an individual time, in particular $b(0)$. That is why the existence proof in Section 4.3 must recover a time-continuous velocity with the stronger spatial Hölder estimate.

localized.intro.positive-curvature|Torus.annotation: For any $v$, the pressure term in the displacement energy is determined by $v\cdot D^2p_{\rm wave}v=-p_{\rm w}F_h'(k\cdot x)(k\cdot v)^2$. If $p_{\rm w}\ge0$, this is at most $(h/2)p_{\rm w}|k|^2|v|^2$. The estimate is one-sided: the large negative value at the center contributes with the favorable sign to the energy in Equation (4.7).

e01.correction.parent-residual|TorusEule.annotation: Frequency truncation leaves an error $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$. In the new expansion $R_U\circ X$ has no dependence on the independent phase $s$, so it is the first mean, $B_2$, that cancels it: $\bar f_2=-\langle H_2\rangle-R_U\circ X$ (see Equation (5.27)). In the momentum of the completed approximation the old defect cancels exactly; the remaining terms come from the finite depth and the time cutoff.

localized.intro.phase-trajectory|TorusEu.annotation: Along the parent, $(\partial_t+U\cdot\nabla)\theta=0$. Adding the leading velocity does not change this identity, since $A_1\cdot\kappa=0$. The completed wave need not be tangent to the phase surfaces: its normal component is determined by Equation (3.6), and the full phase drift is controlled in Lemma 5.10.

localized.intro.time-cutoff|TorusEuler.P.annotation: For $t_0>0$ the cutoff is flat at the activation time, so the seed need only be constructed on $[t_0,T]$. The cutoff does not determine the later initial data of the *mean* correction, which are selected by the two-endpoint problem (see Equation (5.11)). In particular, switching off the oscillation is not the same as switching off the whole velocity increment.

localized.intro.level-profile|TorusEuler.annotation: At level $p\ge2$ the correction $C_p=C[V_{p-1}]$ is known before we form the error to be canceled. It is grouped with the new fields $B_p,V_p$ because of its size, rather than with $V_{p-1}$, the oscillation from which it was computed. This grouping is used to collect the quadratic terms in Equation (5.26).

localized.intro.leading-level|TorusEuler.annotation: The first oscillation and its pressure enter the recursion as data, with $B_1=\bar q_1=0$. The theorem retains this supplied pair; the identification with $\widetilde\chi A_1$ and $\widetilde\chi\mathsf p[A_1]$ is made using Equation (3.7), not by applying the zero-start inverse to the seed.

localized.intro.phase-split|TorusEuler.p.annotation: Write $H_2=\langle H_2\rangle_s+(H_2-\langle H_2\rangle_s)$. The second summand has zero phase integral at each $(t,x)$, as required by Equation (1.12): the phase pressure derivative also has zero integral. The mean equation absorbs the first summand, for which this transverse equation alone cannot provide a centered response.

e01.correction.mean-source|TorusEuler.Hi.annotation: The part of the wave error seen by the mean equation at level two is $\mathbf d\cdot\langle V_1\otimes V_1\rangle_s$ (row divergence in labels), not the full stress of $V_1+C_2$. The fast product of $C_2$ with $V_1$ supplies the term $\langle(\mathbf d\cdot V_1)V_1\rangle_s$ needed to obtain this divergence. Since $V_1=\widetilde\chi g\mathbf a F_h$, the tensor is $\widetilde\chi^2 g^2\langle F_h^2\rangle_s\mathbf a\otimes\mathbf a$. Its negative divergence and $-R_U$ force the mean. The linked algebraic identity assumes the fast-product cancellation proved in Equation (5.25).

e01.correction.mean-equation|TorusEuler..annotation: The first mean error is a slow divergence of a stress. Indeed $\kappa\cdot\partial_s C_2=-\mathbf d\cdot V_1$, so periodic integration by parts replaces $\langle(C_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1\rangle_s$ by $\langle(\mathbf d\cdot V_1)V_1\rangle_s$. Together with $\langle(V_1\cdot\mathbf d)V_1\rangle_s$ this is $\mathbf d\cdot\langle V_1\otimes V_1\rangle_s$. Thus the source contains two velocity factors and a slow derivative rather than a fast derivative of the wave; the parent residual is added separately. (For the higher-level identity, see Equation (5.42).) The linked assembly lemma takes the phase integration by parts as a hypothesis.

e01.correction.mean-endpoints|TorusEuler.annotation: To see the terminal condition, solve Equation (1.5) by variation of constants: $\xi(T,a)=D_aX(T,a)\int_0^T(D_aX(t,a))^{-1}B_2(t,X(t,a))\,dt$. The integral must vanish at each label. The factor $(D_aX(t,a))^{-1}$ converts velocities at different times into the same particle coordinates before they are added.

localized.intro.transverse-equation|Toru.annotation: At level two, $Y_1=V_1$ because $C_1=0$. Consequently Equation (5.28) has precisely one term, $-(B_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$. The expansion specification requires the transverse solution for this force plus $-(H_2-\langle H_2\rangle_s)$, rather than for the centered error alone.

localized.intro.exact-divergence-correct.annotation: The curl completion is not an additional solution of Euler: it is computed directly from the newly determined $V_2$. The condition $C_3=C[V_2]$ in `IsExpansion` enforces that choice; Equation (3.6) gives the exact divergence identity for the pair.

localized.intro.next-level-completion|To.annotation: In Equation (3.5), $\kappa/|\kappa|^2$ contributes $\lambda^{-1}$ up to parent powers. The phase primitive and the slow curl introduce no positive power of $\lambda$. Consequently a completion is smaller than its generating oscillation by $\lambda^{-1}$, although passing from one level to the next requires only $\lambda^{-2/3}$. The extra $\lambda^{-1/3}$ is kept for the estimates of the fast interactions.

e01.correction.retained-completion|Torus.annotation: Truncating the sum by size alone would omit $C_{P+1}$, leaving the slow divergence of $V_P$ uncompensated. In the actual expansion all $P$ oscillations retain their own curl corrections, so divergence vanishes exactly at every finite depth (see Proposition 5.4).

e01.correction.approximate-velocity|Toru.annotation: The construction removes the old momentum defect at the same time as it adds the wave. The mean equation at level two includes $-R_U\circ X$; evaluation at the inverse parent label changes this term back into $-R_U$. The parent equation and the profile equations then give Equation (5.46), with a new residual consisting of the finite hierarchy tail and the time-cutoff term.

e01.correction.cutoff-error|TorusEuler.p.annotation: Let $u=S_\Lambda V$ and $v_\Lambda=u-V$. In the projected momentum equation the new quadratic error is the divergence of $u\otimes u-S_\Lambda(V\otimes V)=v_\Lambda\otimes u+V\otimes v_\Lambda+(I-S_\Lambda)(V\otimes V)$. The first two terms contain the velocity tail; the last is the tail of the product. To estimate the new residual in $C^{1,1/2}$, all three tensors are estimated in $C^{2,1/2}$. This gives $C_P\Lambda^{2-P}\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}}^2$, explaining the power and the square in Equation (5.55). The inherited contribution $\mathbb P S_\Lambda R_V$ is estimated separately.

e01.correction.next-coercivity|TorusEule.annotation: The differentiated momentum equation gives $H^\#=(D^2p_U-\nabla R_U)\circ X$. The sum of the pressure allowances is at most $2/N$, so $H^\#\le I$ if $N\ge4$ and $\|\nabla R_U\|_\infty\le1/2$. In the displacement variable $\xi$, the mean equation has energy $\int_0^T(|\xi_t|^2-H^\#\xi\cdot\xi)\,dt$. The endpoint conditions give $\int|\xi|^2\le(T^2/2)\int|\xi_t|^2$; thus this energy controls $\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$. Returning to label displacements $z=(D_aX)^{-1}\xi$ loses only the factor $D_-^2(1+\|M\|_\infty)^2$ of Section 4. This is why an upper pressure bound, rather than a bound on the full Hessian, suffices.

r5-root-central-gradient-setting|TorusEu.annotation: Oddness keeps the origin a fixed particle in every stage, so the covector and amplitude there solve ordinary differential equations with the central velocity gradient as coefficient. The rank-one part of that gradient must be recovered accurately; the field need not agree with a linear flow on any open neighborhood of zero. (For the central-gradient decomposition, see Equation (6.5).)

e01.parameters.schedule|TorusEuler.Paper.annotation: The gain parameter is the inverse square root of the ratio inherited from wave $j-1$. With the peak of wave $j$ fixed, the relative amplitude during its switch is bounded by $e^{3-L_j}$. Taking $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$ makes this $e^3\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$, which is the scale of the expansion remainder chosen in Section 7.

e01.lemma13.orders|TorusEuler.Paper.lemm.annotation: The restriction on a single increase is used immediately in bounding $K_{j+2}$ in terms of $q_{j+1}$. The divergence of the orders has a later use: for each fixed $m$ the estimates of Section 8 apply from some stage onward with $q_j\ge m$.

e01.lemma13.logarithmic-bound|TorusEuler.annotation: At the stage with parent frequency $\lambda_{j-1}$, three frequency powers intervene before $L_{j+1}$. Their product satisfies $4K_jK_{j+1}K_{j+2}\le4K(q_{j+1}+1)^3\le\log\mathcal B(q_{j+1})\le\log\lambda_{j-1}$. Multiplication by $\log\lambda_{j-1}$ proves Equation (1.15). This is the bound used when estimating powers of the normalized comparison interval.

For each fixed $A$ and $c>0$, Equation (1.15) gives $\mu^{-c}L_{j+1}^A\le\mu^{-c}(\log\mu)^{2A}$, with $\mu=\lambda_{j-1}$. The right side tends to zero uniformly for $\mu\ge N$ as $N\to\infty$. This allows a single initial-frequency threshold in all the comparison estimates at a fixed $C_0$.

affine.wave-equations|TorusEuler.PaperAf.annotation: The structure of Equation (2.1) lets us evolve $k$ first and use its path as a coefficient in the equation for $\mathbf a$. Lean packages these two evolution equations together. Transversality enters separately. The Euler calculation uses it at each time, and the propagation argument obtains it by keeping the initial pairing constant.

c8-frame-trace-scope|TorusEuler.Paper.St.annotation: For nonzero transverse wave data, the derivatives of the axes come from the two wave ODEs evaluated at a single time. Trace zero enters only when the two logarithmic length rates are added and $-B_{11}-B_{22}$ is rewritten as $B_{33}$. Thus the prescribed gradient $B(t)$ and the wave data at $t$ suffice for the frame calculation used in the prescribed-matrix system of Section 2.2.

frame.matrix-entries|TorusEuler.MovingWa.annotation: To read $B_{ij}$, apply $B$ to the input direction $E_j$ and take the output component along $E_i$. For example, the added shear $\sigma E_2\otimes E_1$ has its only nonzero entry at $(2,1)$ because it sends $E_1$ to $\sigma E_2$. This fixes which entry changes when the preceding wave is added to the older gradient in Section 2.2.1.

frame.strength-couplings|TorusEuler.hasD.annotation: Dividing the pressure term $p_{\rm w}k$ in Equation (2.1) by $|\mathbf a|$ gives $2\nu E_1$. Thus $B_{12}$ contributes both through $-B\mathbf a$ and through pressure, while the $E_3$ component of $-B\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|$ is $-\eta$. These two components turn the amplitude direction in the frame identities below.

frame.derivative-identities|TorusEuler.P.annotation: In the formal statement, `WaveOn` supplies the two differential equations and the pressure coefficient. Nonvanishing and $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$ are supplied separately at every time in the set, where the three axes and their derivatives are evaluated. The propagation argument for Equation (2.1) supplies these pointwise hypotheses when the data are nonzero and transverse at launch and $B$ is smooth on the interval.

r5-reference-small-ratio-gain|TorusEuler.annotation: The reference normal reaches $\varphi=\pi/4$ at $\tau=\sqrt{2/\varepsilon}$. Up to that time, $\cos\varphi\ge1/\sqrt2$, so the integral in Equation (2.14) already contributes at least $\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ to the logarithm of the amplitude. The factor $\sqrt{\cos\varphi}$ costs only $\tfrac14\log2$ at that time. The peak occurs later, on the scale $\varepsilon^{-1}$.

In the parameter schedule a wave of index $j\ge2$ inherits $\varepsilon=L_j^{-2}$, with $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. The first-unit bound becomes $e^3\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$. The time cutoff costs a derivative of size $Cr$, but the induction has $Ce^3r\le\lambda_{j-1}$; thus the activation error is already small on the scale of the following frequency, not just the frequency of the wave being added (see Equation (7.10)).

r5-reference-reference-system-overview|T.annotation: The strong-shear limit must be taken in the scaled equations. For instance, the preceding shear contributes $\sigma_p(k\cdot E_2)(\mathbf a\cdot E_1)$ to the pressure numerator. In units of $\nu\lambda$ this is $2(\sigma_p/\sigma)\zeta_2\alpha_1$. It remains an order-one coefficient even though the corresponding two physical projections carry factors $S^{-1}$. At reference inputs it produces the damping term in Equation (2.5).

r5-reference-additive-overview|TorusEule.annotation: The interval must contain the prescribed crossing, which can occur on the normalized scale $(\varepsilon\varepsilon_+)^{-1/2}$.
