The time integral of the latter has length at most one. By Lemma D.2(c) and Equation (D.2) the weighted positive-order Hölder norms of these coefficients are bounded by a parent power times $\ell_*^{1/2}$. Choose the radius exponent to pay for the inverse bound $A$ in Equation (5.13); this works at all orders without requiring $K$ or $\Omega$ themselves to be small.

e03-appd-exact-order-norm|TorusEuler.app.annotation: Here $|c|_m$ is a sum over derivatives of exact order $m$. In particular $|c|_0$ need not be small when the positive-order terms of the finite norm are small. This distinction is used in Equation (D.7), which involves only $m\ge1$.

e03-r2-appd-holder-interpolation|TorusEu.annotation: Apply the geometric-mean bound to every derivative of order $m$ and sum. Cauchy–Schwarz pairs the order-$m$ supremum sum with the order-$(m+1)$ sum. This is the interpolation step used in the proof of Equation (D.2), whose stated conclusion is the finite-norm comparison.

e03-appd-derivative-product|TorusEuler.P.annotation: In Equation (D.3), the label and phase shifts cost different inverse lengths. In Equation (D.4), the product keeps its full derivative budget, because the weight and every derivative split between the factors. The theorem also supplies boundedness of the output families, under the corresponding bounded input derivatives.

r5-app-coefficient-hypotheses|TorusEuler.annotation: The exponent $C$ is fixed for a coefficient, and the numbers $C_m$ may depend on the order. The bounds in Equation (D.6) are uniform in time but concern only derivatives in $a$. In particular they do not bound derivatives in time; those are obtained separately in the auxiliary note.

e03-appd-inverse-coeff|TorusEuler.Paper..annotation: Take $C$ to dominate both the exponent for $c$ and the bound $|c^{-1}|\le\mathsf D^C$. A term with $k$ positive derivatives of $c$ (of total order $m$) contains $k+1$ inverse factors, hence has power at most $\mathsf D^{C(m+2k+1)}\le\mathsf D^{C(3m+1)}$. This proves Equation (D.6) with exponent $3C$; the formal theorem chooses $C=\max(a,e)$ for the integer input exponents and works in a complete real normed algebra.

e03-appd-radius-coeff|TorusEuler.Paper.S.annotation: Lemma D.2(c) is stronger than boundedness of the scaled coefficient norm: for $m\ge1$ it retains $\ell_*^m|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{2a}\ell_*$ with integer $a$ in Lean. The zero-order term has size $C_0\mathsf D^a$ and is not part of the smallness condition. If an exponent is enlarged after multiplication or inversion, impose the radius restriction with the new exponent.

e03-appd-lifting-equation|TorusEuler.pap.annotation: Lemma D.3 is an a priori estimate for a solution of the given equation, not a construction of the inverse. Its input is a zero-order estimate valid throughout the admissible space (for the mean equation, the endpoint inverse of Theorem 4.2 supplies it). Its output is the finite derivative estimate with that same inverse cost, using commutation for the constant operators and the product rule for the coefficient actions.

e03-appd-lifting-equation|TorusEuler.Pap.annotation: For the mean the constraint belongs to the displacement $z$, with $z(0)=z(T)=0$ and $v=z_t$. The integrated equation contains $Kv$ and the time integral of $\Omega v$, modulo a label gradient. Taking a label derivative preserves the constraints and produces the same integrated equation for the differentiated unknown, with a new forcing. The inverse from the preceding section supplies existence; Lemma D.3 estimates such solutions.

e03-r2-appd-constraint-subspace|TorusEul.annotation: The differentiation must preserve the space on which the zero-order inverse is available. In the mean problem, label derivatives preserve both the divergence constraint and the endpoint values of the displacement. In the transverse problem this is why one works in fixed coordinates as in Equation (5.18): direct differentiation of $\kappa\cdot V=0$ introduces the inhomogeneous constraint $\kappa\cdot\partial_{a_i}V=-(\partial_{a_i}\kappa)\cdot V$.

e03-appd-low-order|TorusEuler.Paper.Stat.annotation: “For every admissible source” means the same nonnegative $C_{\rm low}$ bounds every unknown in the solution space with its own forcing and prescribed data. Under Equation (D.7) through order $n$, the statement bounds the order-$n$ solution norm by $C_n C_{\rm low}$ times the order-$n$ norm of the forcing and data.

e03-r2-appd-lifting-operator-norm|TorusE.annotation: For the mean, time integration costs at most $T\le1$ in the spatial Hölder norm. The coefficient action also includes multiplication by the differentiated coefficient and, if the equation is projected, the Leray projection. In the formal abstraction $b_\nu$ bounds the whole bilinear action in the chosen zero-order seminorms, so every such fixed operator cost must be included before using Equation (D.7).

e03-appd-slow-bound|TorusEuler.appendixS.annotation: For a particular weighted derivative of $c_\nu$ of order $i\ge1$, its norm times $b_\nu C_{\rm low}$ is at most the whole nonnegative sum in Equation (D.7). The word used by the formal proof is one coordinate multi-index after commuting the directions. This gives a bound $C_i$ for each product-rule term, without requiring the coefficients themselves to be small.

e03-appd-slow-bound|TorusEuler.paperLemm.annotation: A derivative of total order at most $n$ can put between one and $n$ derivatives on a coefficient. Every one of these terms is covered by Equation (D.7). The formal word estimate only needs the bound on each such term; it follows from the summed bound by nonnegativity.

e03-appd-slow-bound|TorusEuler.Paper.Sta.annotation: In the differentiated equation the product with zero derivatives on $c_\nu$ belongs to the same operator on the new unknown. It is not a term to be bounded perturbatively. Only the terms with $i\ge1$ derivatives on $c_\nu$ are put on the right, and Equation (D.7) pays for the inverse on these terms.

e03-appd-lifted-conclusion|TorusEuler.pa.annotation: For a scaled first derivative the estimate has the form $V_1\le C_{\rm low}F_1+C_1V_0$. The second coefficient is $C_1$, rather than another uncontrolled inverse norm, because Equation (D.7) already includes $C_{\rm low}$. Substituting $V_0\le C_{\rm low}F_0$ gives a single inverse factor. The same argument at order $n$ involves only strictly lower orders of $v$ on the right.

e03-appd-lifted-conclusion|TorusEuler.Pa.annotation:
In the recursion following differentiation, the coefficient of the lower-order norm of $v$ is $C_{m low}\sum_
u b_
u\ell_*^i|c_
u|_i$, with $i\ge1$. Under Equation (D.7) it is an order constant. Thus induction involves powers of these constants, not successive powers of the inverse norm.

The high-order estimate retains the parent cost of the original inverse. The proof is valid for any finite family of commuting derivatives with the stipulated product rules and seminorms. With the paper's scaled label and phase directions it gives the displayed finite-order bound under Equation (D.7).

e03-r2-appd-lifting-constant-dependence|.annotation: The constant in the lifted estimate is fixed by the derivative order and the bounds in Equation (D.7). It is not required to be uniform as the order increases. What must be uniform is the power of the parent in $C_{\rm low}$: the new order-dependent constants can enter $\mathcal B$, whereas a new parent power at every hierarchy level would not be paid for by the fixed frequency margin.

e03-r2-appd-lifting-holder-case|TorusEul.annotation: Use the zero-order inverse in $C^{0,1/2}$, the Hölder product inequality, and Equation (D.7) with $|c_\nu|_{m,1/2}$. The same recurrence follows. The extra cost of passing from supremum bounds to these Hölder hypotheses is paid separately by Equation (D.2), not by the lifting induction.

e03-appd-weights|TorusEuler.appendixFini.annotation: Since $\ell_*$ and $h$ are constant in label and phase, a product-rule term with $i$ label derivatives on the coefficient carries $\ell_*^i$ there and $\ell_*^{|\beta|-i}h^j$ on the unknown. No phase derivative can hit the phase-independent coefficient. This allocates exactly the weight needed by Equation (D.7).

e03-appd-induction|TorusEuler.paperLemma.annotation: After the coefficient sum is bounded by Equation (D.7), the recurrence has the form $V_n\le C_{\rm low}F_n+C_nV_{n-1}$. Since $F_{n-1}\le F_n$, substituting the induction bound for $V_{n-1}$ leaves a single factor $C_{\rm low}$. The remaining constant may grow with order, but it is independent of the parent size.

e03-appd-induction|TorusEuler.Paper.Proo.annotation: Although the zero-order inverse estimate is applied at every order, in the recurrence its additional occurrences are multiplied by the quantities bounded in Equation (D.7). Substituting the lower-order estimates therefore leaves a single $C_{\rm low}$ in front of the source norm. The constants depending on derivative order may enter $\mathcal B$ without changing the parent exponent.

c8-coefficient-radius-gain|TorusEuler.Pa.annotation: The term needed here is the second estimate of Lemma D.2(c), not the bound for the full coefficient norm. For $m\ge1$, $\ell_*^m|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{2C}\ell_*$. The factor $\ell_*$ has been kept precisely because the differentiated coefficient will be multiplied by another inverse bound.

c8-holder-radius-gain|TorusEuler.Paper.P.annotation: The positive-order estimate of Lemma D.2(c) gives a factor $\ell_*$ in both $\ell_*^m|c|_m$ and $\ell_*^{m+1}|c|_{m+1}$ when $m\ge1$. The cost $\ell_*^{-1/2}$ in Equation (D.2) leaves $\ell_*^{1/2}$. This is the gain in Equation (5.13) for $K$ and $\Omega$, whose zero-order inverse is a Hölder estimate.

c8-common-envelope-exponent|TorusEuler.P.annotation: Suppose the weighted positive-order coefficient bound is $C_m\mathsf D^C\ell_*^{1/2}$ and the inverse costs $\mathsf D^{C_A}$. With $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ their product is at most $C_m\mathsf D^{C+C_A-a/2}$. Choose $a\ge2(C+C_A)$, also large enough for Lemma D.2(c). The same radius then pays for all orders, since $m$ occurs only in $C_m$.

e03-r2-aux-threshold-growth|TorusEuler.I.annotation: Distinguish the fixed time order $q$ from the scheduled spatial order $q_j$. At step $j$ the expansion depth is $P=6K(q_{j+1})$. For any fixed $q$, $P+q+2\le7K(q_{j+1})$ eventually. The inequality in Equation (1.1) of the auxiliary note then bounds the corresponding paper constants by $\mu=\lambda_{j-1}$. The formal threshold also includes the additional finite reserve needed to build the intermediate levels.

e03-aux-mixed-quantifiers|TorusEuler.Pap.annotation: The generalized form of auxiliary Lemma 1.2 asks for the mixed bounds for every qualifying construction rather than for the selected one. It is an unproved target. The selected-construction theorem proves precisely the eventual estimates required for the convergence argument here.

e03-aux-mixed-display|TorusEuler.Schedul.annotation: For nearby times apply the half-Hölder interpolation inequality to the difference $\partial_t^qf(t)-\partial_t^qf(t')$ and its spatial derivatives. Smoothness of the stage on the compact slab gives uniform continuity through order $m+1$. It follows that the $C^{m,1/2}$ difference tends to zero as $t'\to t$, including at either time endpoint. This establishes continuity in the norm used in Equation (1.2) of the auxiliary note.

e03-aux-time-quantifiers|TorusEuler.Pape.annotation: The generalized form of auxiliary Lemma 1.3 quantifies over every construction with the threshold and step data. It is recorded as unproved and unused. The selected version proves existence of the common integer exponent and starting index for each fixed time order, which is all the induction uses.

e03-aux-time-display|TorusEuler.auxiliar.annotation: The residual rate is tied to the *next* wave. For the parent $U_{j-1}$ of step $j$, Equation (1.3) of the auxiliary note gives $\|\partial_t^i R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda_j^{-5/2}$. This is the scale of the stress quadratic in the leading velocity of size $\lambda_j^{-5/4}$. In the induction the parent residual retains this factor through time order $q-1$, not merely a small power of the old frequency.

e03-aux-time-display|TorusEuler.Paper.Au.annotation: This condition combines the two numerical bounds through order $q$ at a single stage with continuity in the uniform spatial norm. The exponent is a nonnegative integer. Auxiliary Lemma 1.3 additionally proves that some such exponent works from a sufficiently late index onward.

e03-aux-induction-on-time|TorusEuler.Ind.annotation: For $q=0$ both estimates are already consequences of Theorem M.7.1. For the induction step, use the time bounds in Equation (1.3) of the auxiliary note at order $q-1$ on the old parent, obtain the mixed correction estimate in Equation (1.2) at order $q$, and then establish the bound in Equation (1.3) at order $q$ for the new stage. The numerical induction theorem assumes the analytic child-step implication; the subsequent estimates establish it for the selected construction.

e03-aux-induction-on-time|TorusEuler.Pap.annotation: The implication for the generalized form of auxiliary Lemma 1.3 assumes a uniform analytic time-step estimate for arbitrary qualifying constructions. That hypothesis remains open, so this implication does not prove the generalized lemma unconditionally. The selected-construction proof establishes the bounds along its own sequence.

The analogous implication for auxiliary Lemma 1.2 assumes the order-growth result, generalized velocity-residual time bounds and a uniform correction step. The open generalized time-step hypotheses are not used in the selected-construction proof. That proof gives the mixed bound directly along the selected sequence.

e03-aux-base-mixed|TorusEuler.InductiveE.annotation: At time order zero the mixed correction is the second estimate of Equation (M.7.4). For fixed $m$, the inequality holds when $q_j\ge m$, which eventually follows from order growth. The linked result supplies the numerical Hölder bound; continuity of the correction curve is separate.

e03-aux-parent-mixed-bounds|TorusEuler.I.annotation: For $i\le q$, obtain the new velocity time derivative from the projected equation and then apply Bernstein in space. For $R_U$ use the preceding time-order estimate only, through $q-1$. The linked theorem obtains the powers in Equation (2.1) of the auxiliary note; its common constants are chosen after the time order and input exponent, while the separate Bernstein theorem gives the sharper independence of the residual constant.

e03-aux-parent-mixed-bounds|TorusEuler.S.annotation: The induction hypothesis on the old slab restricts to $[0,S_j]$. The projected equation supplies order $q$ of $U$, but Equation (2.1) of the auxiliary note retains order $q-1$ for $R_U$. Bernstein in the old band contributes $\Lambda_U^n=\mu^{5n}$ to each line. It does not replace the new-frequency factor $\lambda^{-5/2}$ in the second line by an old-frequency power.

e03-aux-no-high-residual-jet|TorusEuler..annotation: The old residual appears in the mean equation at level two, not in the centered transverse source. This is essential: the induction knows the old residual only through time order $q-1$. The mean equation gains the missing time derivative by Equation (2.3) of the auxiliary note; subsequent sources use the resulting mean velocity $B_2$, not its forcing or its pressure.

e03-r2-aux-mean-time-gain-display|TorusE.annotation: The integrated endpoint inverse first bounds the actual $v=z_t$; it determines its initial trace from the two conditions on $z$. The fixed-time inverse of $\mathbb P(K(t)\cdot)$ then bounds each higher time derivative from the differentiated strong equation, using Equation (M.D.3) in Hölder norms. This gives Equation (2.3) of the auxiliary note, with one extra label derivative on the source but one fewer time derivative. Lean chooses the minimum radius exponent before the time order (its index $q$ on the right corresponds to $q+1$ on the left), so the construction need not be changed for higher time orders.

e03-r2-aux-residual-time-source-bound|To.annotation: At level two the mean source consists of the averaged quadratic stress of the leading wave and the transported parent residual. Both have scale $\lambda^{-5/2}$ up to old-parent powers. The average removes the fast phase derivative in the stress. By Equation (2.2) of the auxiliary note the residual has the required time norm through $q-1$; this is precisely the order needed by Equation (2.3) of the auxiliary note to bound the mean velocity through $q$.

e03-aux-recurrence-smallness|TorusEuler..annotation: The level-two source target is $\lambda^{-5/4-2/3}=\lambda^{-23/12}$. Of the three direct source powers $-9/4,-5/2,-2$, the last is closest to the target and leaves $\lambda^{-1/12}$. The same spare power occurs after the level-two mean estimate. At later levels the common factor $\lambda^{-2(p-2)/3}$ is present on both sides. Since $\lambda=\mu^{K_j}$, any fixed parent cost $C\mu^A$ is eventually absorbed by $\lambda^{-1/12}$. Independence of $A$ from $p$ is essential: the induction must absorb the parent powers at each level rather than carry them into the next, as in the proof of Equation (M.5.40).

e03-aux-physical-time-estimates|TorusEul.annotation: To read the $q$th Eulerian time jet, expand the transport identity repeatedly. Each term has one profile jet with at most $q$ extra spatial derivatives and products of old-parent jets. If the $n$ further spatial derivatives split as $n_1+n_2=n$, the parent factors cost at most $\lambda^{n_1}$ and the profile at most $\lambda^{2(n_2+q+1)}$, apart from fixed parent powers. Hence the exponent in Equation (2.5) of the auxiliary note can be written $2(n+1)+\psi'_q$ with $\psi'_q$ independent of $n$. The formal reserve is $(P+q+1)+3P\le H$.

e03-aux-cutoff-commutation|TorusEuler.Tr.annotation: At step $j$ the operator $S_{\Lambda_j}$ is fixed throughout the slab. Therefore $\partial_t^q(S_{\Lambda_j}-\operatorname{Id})V=(S_{\Lambda_j}-\operatorname{Id})\partial_t^qV$. This permits direct application of Equation (M.B.2) to each time jet of the uncut approximation; no derivative of the symbol or scale appears.

e03-aux-add-half-bounds|TorusEuler.Trunc.annotation: Both terms in the exact correction identity are estimated in the same mixed norm: the mean by Equation (2.4) of the auxiliary note, without any fast phase cost, and the Fourier tail by Equation (M.B.2) applied to the time jet. Their bounds are each $\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$. Thus the estimate for the correction is global even though the oscillation it excludes is localized. Norm continuity on the closed slab is obtained separately.

e03-aux-new-velocity-power|TorusEuler.Tr.annotation: At $n=0$, Equation (2.5) of the auxiliary note bounds the time jet of $V$ by $\lambda^{2+\psi'_q}$. The uniform cutoff bound costs at most another factor $\lambda$ eventually. This yields $\psi_q=\psi'_q+3$ for all $i\le q$, as required in Equation (1.3) of the auxiliary note.

e03-aux-all-jets-terminal-limit|TorusEul.annotation: Fix a closed spatial ball separated from the lattice. For any finite joint order $k$, take a starting stage valid for all mixed orders up to $k$. Expanding each joint derivative into time and space directions gives at most $2^k$ mixed terms. By Lemma 1.2 of the auxiliary note applied to those mixed derivatives, the increments are bounded by $2^k\lambda_j^{-1}$, and hence are summable. On the closed cylinder the uniform convergence of the fields and each successive derivative identifies the limits as derivatives of the same field, by integration along line segments, including one-sided derivatives at the time faces.

e03-r2-aux-generalized-auxiliary-conclus.annotation: The linked conditional proof takes the main stage and limit results together with the generalized mixed-increment assertion as hypotheses, then applies the extension argument. The generalized form of auxiliary Lemma 1.2 remains an open antecedent. The selected theorem proves the mixed estimates along the chosen sequence and establishes the existence statement of Remark 1.2 independently of that stronger antecedent.
